name: Pitztaler Gletscher
kurzbeschreibung: The highest-altitude glacier ski area in Tirol, offering year-round skiing, breathtaking views, and the famous Gletscherexpress cable car.
beschreibung:
Overview

Celebrated as the "Roof of Tyrol," the Pitztaler Gletscher represents the highest glaciated ski domain and alpine observation destination in all of Austria. Located at the very head of the Pitztal valley near Mittelberg, this colossal amphitheater of ice and granite rises into the permanent snowline at an astounding 3,440 meters elevation. The ascent begins with a remarkable engineering feat: the subterranean "Gletscherexpress" funicular ascends through deep solid rock, surmounting over 1,100 vertical meters in just eight minutes to the glacier plateau at 2,840 meters. From there, the futuristic Wildspitzbahn gondola glides silently to the crest of the Hinterer Brunnenkogel (3,440 m). Perched directly on the precipice is the architectural wonder Café 3.440—Austria's highest coffeehouse—featuring a dramatic glass-cantilevered observation deck suspended over the abyss, framing unmatched panoramas of over 50 glaciated 3,000-meter giants and the 3,774-meter Wildspitze, North Tyrol's highest summit.

Route & Requirements

Despite the extreme alpine altitude, cutting-edge cableway technology delivers safe, barrier-free access for sightseers and families alike. From the upper gondola terminal, level indoor and outdoor walkways lead directly into Café 3.440 and onto the viewing platform (easy grade T1, wheelchair accessible). During summer, mountain hikers explore marked alpine routes across the moraine plateau, such as the Glacier Interpretive Trail or the traverse to the historic Braunschweiger Hütte (2,759 m; challenging boulder-strewn alpine trek, 2 hours, grade T3). For seasoned mountaineers, the glacier serves as the primary springboard for ascending the Wildspitze: this rigorous glacier climb navigates heavily crevassed terrain requiring crampons, ice axes, rope-team protocols, and certified mountain guide leadership. At elevations exceeding 3,400 meters, thin air necessitates gradual acclimatization. Heavy thermal outerwear, gloves, and category 4 UV-blocking glacier glasses are mandatory even in mid-July. Leashed and muzzled dogs may ride the lifts, but high-alpine glacier traverses are impassable for pets.

Visit & Arrival

Travelers arrive by rail via mainline ÖBB trains to Imst-Pitztal railway station. From the station forecourt, frequent regional VVT bus line 4204 runs the length of the valley directly to the Mittelberg/Gletscherexpress terminus. Motorists exit the Inntal autobahn A12 at Imst/Pitztal and follow provincial highway L16 south for 35 kilometers to the valley head. Ample free parking is situated at the Mittelberg base terminal.

Tips

Indulge in artisanal stone pine cake (Zirbentorte) and hot espresso inside Café 3.440 while observing roped mountaineering parties ascending the sheer ice flanks of the Wildspitze. Before boarding the funicular, visit the serene "Chapel of White Light," a minimalist alpine sanctuary sculpted from pale Tyrolean granite by artist Heinz Pflaundler.
preis: Bergbahn Berg- und Talfahrt (Gletscherexpress + Wildspitzbahn) ca. 45–48 €
